fixes.explanation: Evil, baker. Moses has just asked Aaron what this people did to him that he led them into so great a sin (Exodus 32:21). Aaron's reply starts, "Do not be enraged, my lord." Then comes the line you picked: "You yourself know that the people are intent on evil." (Exodus 32:22) After that he tells Moses what the people said to him (Exodus 32:23).

Sandals, friend? Nobody asks for those here. Aaron asks for gold earrings, the ones on their wives and sons and daughters (Exodus 32:2). Shoes never come up. I'd say that's one request you'd remember if you were standing in that line.

A wall, baker? That's not what Aaron builds. The text says he built an altar before the calf (Exodus 32:5). Then he proclaimed, "Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD." Walls keep things out. This altar is set up so offerings can be brought, and the next day they bring burnt offerings and peace offerings (Exodus 32:6).

That's not what Moses says, friend. He asks, "Why should the Egyptians declare, ‘He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them from the face of the earth’?" (Exodus 32:12) The Egyptians' words are about evil intent, not about their gods winning. Then Moses asks the LORD to relent from doing harm.

Singing, baker. Joshua hears the people shouting and says to Moses, "The sound of war is in the camp." But Moses replies, "It is neither the cry of victory nor the cry of defeat; I hear the sound of singing!" (Exodus 32:17-18) Joshua took the shouting for war, and Moses names it as singing. I think Joshua was about to get a very different kind of news.
